p: A Tuesday browse along Station Road fits nicely into a bigger look at one of Northumberland's most interesting towns. Ashington grew up around coal, with collieries and pit terraces shaping the place for generations. That heritage hasn't gone anywhere: it shapes the streets, the community spirit and the stories you'll hear from people who've lived here all their lives.

The place to dig deeper is Woodhorn, on the edge of town. The old colliery buildings now house a museum and the Northumberland Archives, and it's also home to the collection of the Pitmen Painters, the group of Ashington miners who took up painting in the 1930s and ended up with their work shown far beyond the North East. Their story became a hit stage play, and seeing the paintings in the place where those men worked is genuinely moving. Right next door, the Queen Elizabeth II Country Park has a big lake with a path round it, perfect for a gentle walk, a picnic or a bit of duck spotting with the kids.

Football fans might like to know that Ashington produced some proper legends, including Jackie Milburn and the Charlton brothers, Jack and Bobby. A short drive east takes you to Newbiggin-by-the-Sea, where the bronze Couple sculpture stands out in the bay. Pair a market morning with lunch in town and a bracing seaside walk, and you've got a cracking, low-cost day out.
